intent: I've got a Flask backend on port 3000 (cd backend && python server.py) and a Vite frontend on 5173 (cd frontend && npm run dev). Neither is running. How do I get a playwright test to run against both at once?
rubric: Shows how to call with_server.py with two --server/--port pairs followed by `-- python test.py` (running --help first), and gives a Playwright-only automation script that uses headless Chromium, waits for networkidle, and closes the browser.

intent: My React app runs with `npm run dev` on port 5173 and it isn't running yet. Write me a Playwright script that checks the login form: fill in email and password, click submit, and confirm the dashboard heading shows up. Also tell me how to run it.
rubric: Gives a Python sync_playwright script that launches Chromium headless, waits for networkidle after goto, runs the login flow, checks the dashboard heading, and closes the browser, and says to run it through scripts/with_server.py (checking --help first) with --server "npm run dev" --port 5173 instead of putting server startup in the script.

intent: The app's already up at localhost:8080 but I have no idea what the buttons or inputs are called in the DOM, it's all generated by some component library. How should I approach automating the 'create project' flow?
rubric: Describes reconnaissance-then-action: go to the page, wait for networkidle, take a full-page screenshot and/or read page.content() and list locators like buttons and inputs, choose selectors from what actually rendered, then do the actions, with an example headless sync script.

intent: I don't want to depend on some helper script. Just give me one self-contained Python file that starts my `npm run dev` server itself on port 5173, waits for it, runs a playwright check that the homepage title is right, then kills the server.
rubric: Gives one self-contained Python file that starts `npm run dev` with subprocess, polls port 5173 until it's ready, runs the Playwright title check, and always shuts the server down in a finally block, without relying on with_server.py.

intent: i have a plain static index.html with a contact form, no js framework, no server. how would you write a playwright test that fills it out and checks the thank-you message appears?
rubric: Treats the page as static: identifies selectors by reading the HTML, loads it with a file:// URL in a headless sync Playwright script, fills and submits the form, checks the thank-you message, and falls back to dynamic handling if the HTML alone isn't enough.

intent: Need to capture browser console errors while clicking around my local dashboard at http://localhost:4000 (already running). Can you give me a script that logs everything the console prints and saves a screenshot at the end?
rubric: Gives a Python sync Playwright script that registers a page.on('console') handler before navigating, launches Chromium headless, waits for networkidle, does the interactions, saves a screenshot, prints or saves the collected logs, and closes the browser.

intent: My Playwright script keeps saying it can't find elements, but when I open the page manually they're obviously there. It's a Vue SPA. Here's what I do: page.goto('http://localhost:5173'); print(page.locator('button').all()). What's wrong?
rubric: Explains that the DOM is being inspected before the SPA has finished rendering, and fixes it by adding page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle') (and wait_for_selector where needed) before inspecting, with a corrected headless script that closes the browser.

intent: Our whole test suite is async Python using pytest-asyncio, so please give me an async_playwright version of a test that checks the nav menu links on localhost:3000 all load. No sync API please, it won't fit in with the rest of our code.
rubric: Uses async_playwright with async/await in a form that works under pytest-asyncio, and doesn't use the sync API, while still checking every nav link on localhost:3000 loads.

intent: Quick q — there's a scripts/with_server.py helper in this testing toolkit. Should I open it up and read how it works before using it for my Next.js app on port 3000?
rubric: Says to run `python scripts/with_server.py --help` first and use the script as a black box, reading the source only if a custom solution turns out to be truly necessary, and shows an example call with --server "npm run dev" --port 3000 -- python script.py.

intent: Write a Playwright script to test the checkout flow on my local shop at localhost:5173 (already running). I want to actually SEE the browser while it runs so I can watch what's happening. Don't make it headless.
rubric: The script launches Chromium in headed mode (headless=False, optionally with slow_mo) so I can watch the checkout flow, and it still waits for the page to load properly and closes the browser at the end.
